titleEn: A quarter of the world’s reptiles use rocky habitats. So why aren’t we protecting them?
titleZh: 四分之一的爬行动物依赖岩石生境，为何保护仍然不足？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Ask any reptile lover where to find a cold-blooded creature and chances are they will point to a rocky outcrop.
paragraphs.zh: 问任何一个爬行动物爱好者在哪里可以找到一个冷血动物，他们很可能会指出一个岩石露头。

paragraphs.en: Look closely and you might find a snake or lizard basking on a sun-warmed boulder, sheltering in a narrow crevice or even living under a loose surface rock.
paragraphs.zh: 仔细观察，你可能会发现一条蛇或蜥蜴在阳光温暖的巨石上晒太阳，躲在狭窄的裂缝中，甚至生活在松散的岩石表面下。

paragraphs.en: For reptiles, these rocks are not simply somewhere to hang out.
paragraphs.zh: 对于爬行动物来说，这些岩石不仅仅是它们的栖息地。

paragraphs.en: Rocky habitats help reptiles control their body temperature, escape predators and survive harsh winters. They are also a refuge where reptiles can socialise, lay eggs and find food.
paragraphs.zh: 岩石栖息地帮助爬行动物控制体温，躲避捕食者，度过严冬。它们也是爬行动物进行社交、产卵和寻找食物的避难所。

paragraphs.en: Without rocky habitats, many reptile species would struggle to survive, putting wider ecosystems at risk of collapse. But how many reptile species actually depend on rocky habitats?
paragraphs.zh: 如果没有岩石栖息地，许多爬行动物物种将难以生存，使更广泛的生态系统面临崩溃的风险。但有多少爬行动物物种真正依赖于岩石栖息地？

paragraphs.en: Our new study aimed both to answer this question and identify what threats rock-dwelling species face.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的新研究旨在回答这个问题，并确定岩石栖息物种面临的威胁。

paragraphs.en: Rocky habitats at risk
paragraphs.zh: 岩石栖息地处于危险之中

paragraphs.en: Rocky habitats are found on every continent, ranging from cliff faces to outcrops and even areas covered with loose, scattered rocks.
paragraphs.zh: 岩石栖息地在每个大陆上都有，从悬崖面到露头，甚至是覆盖着松散、分散的岩石的地区。

paragraphs.en: Rocky habitats may seem relatively indestructible compared to forests or other living habitats. In reality, they are easily damaged or destroyed and, once lost, may take centuries or even millenia to reform.
paragraphs.zh: 与森林或其他生物栖息地相比，岩石栖息地似乎相对坚不可摧。但实际上，它们很容易遭到破坏或摧毁，一旦失去，可能需要几个世纪甚至几千年的时间才能改革。

paragraphs.en: Today, one in five reptile species is at risk of extinction. Habitat loss is the most pressing threat to reptile populations worldwide.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，每五种爬行动物中就有一种濒临灭绝。栖息地的丧失是世界范围内爬行动物种群面临的最紧迫威胁。

paragraphs.en: Rocky areas are under pressure from threats such as mining, quarrying and urbanisation. In the United Arab Emirates, for instance, rapid urban development threatens the last isolated rock formation known to support the critically endangered Emirati leaf-toed gecko (Asaccus caudivolvulus).
paragraphs.zh: 岩石地区面临着采矿、采石和城市化等威胁。例如，在阿拉伯联合酋长国，快速的城市发展威胁到了最后一个孤立的岩层，该岩层是极度濒危的阿联酋叶趾壁虎（Asaccus caudivolvulus）的栖息地。

paragraphs.en: Rock crushing is another problem. It involves using specialised machinery to turn boulderfields and other rocky habitats into farmland. In Australia, new rock crushing machinery can clear and crush surface rocks at rates of up to one hectare per hour. These methods are increasingly being used in agricultural areas in Western Australia, South Australia and western Victoria, threatening the habitat of several threatened reptile species.
paragraphs.zh: 岩石破碎是另一个问题。它涉及到使用专门的机械将巨石地和其他岩石栖息地变成农田。在澳大利亚，新的岩石破碎机械可以以每小时一公顷的速度清理和破碎地表岩石。这些方法越来越多地用于西澳大利亚州，南澳和西维多利亚的农业地区，威胁到几种受威胁的爬行动物物种的栖息地。

paragraphs.en: Despite their importance, rocky habitats are often overlooked in conservation plans and initiatives, such as the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s (IUCN) habitat classification system.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管它们很重要，但岩石栖息地在保护计划和倡议中经常被忽视，例如国际自然保护联盟（IUCN）的栖息地分类系统。

paragraphs.en: What we studied
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究的内容

paragraphs.en: Our research team led the first-ever study to measure the global importance of rocky habitats for reptiles.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究团队领导了有史以来第一项研究，以衡量岩石栖息地对爬行动物的全球重要性。

paragraphs.en: We reviewed IUCN data and found over a quarter of the world’s terrestrial snakes, lizards and worm-lizards like the pink-tailed worm-lizard (Aprasia parapulchella) use rock habitats. More than 1,000 species – roughly 10% of the world’s reptile species – completely depend on rocky habitats for their survival.
paragraphs.zh: 我们查阅了世界自然保护联盟的数据，发现世界上超过四分之一的陆生蛇、蜥蜴和蠕虫蜥蜴（如粉红尾蠕虫蜥蜴（Aprasia paramphichella））都生活在岩石栖息地。超过1,000种爬行动物（约占世界爬行动物物种的10%）完全依赖岩石栖息地生存。

paragraphs.en: We found rock-dependent species had geographic ranges that were 68% smaller, on average, than species that don’t rely on rocky habitats. They were also 51% more likely to be classified as critically endangered.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，依赖岩石的物种的地理范围平均比不依赖岩石栖息地的物种小68%，它们被列为极度濒危物种的可能性也高出51%。

paragraphs.en: From an evolutionary perspective, these species are also unique. Species across the reptile family tree, from worm-lizards to geckos and snakes, have independently adapted to rocky environments. But many rock-dependent reptiles are restricted to extremely isolated habitats so, if these areas are damaged or destroyed, they have few places to go.
paragraphs.zh: 从进化的角度来看，这些物种也是独一无二的。爬行动物家族树上的物种，从蠕虫蜥蜴到壁虎和蛇，都独立地适应了岩石环境。但许多依赖岩石的爬行动物被限制在极其孤立的栖息地，所以，如果这些地区被破坏或摧毁，它们几乎没有地方可去。

paragraphs.en: Importantly, we found more than twice as many reptiles live in rocky areas than is captured under current classifications. This matters because without proper recognition, these habitats are less likely to be prioritised for conservation.
paragraphs.zh: 重要的是，我们发现生活在岩石地区的爬行动物数量是目前分类中捕获的爬行动物数量的两倍多。这很重要，因为如果没有适当的认识，这些栖息地就不太可能被优先保护。

paragraphs.en: So, what can we do?
paragraphs.zh: 那我们能做什么呢？

paragraphs.en: Rocky areas are biodiversity hotspots that will only become more important as the world warms, serving as crucial climate refuges that protect animals from drought and extreme temperatures.
paragraphs.zh: 岩石地区是生物多样性的热点，随着世界变暖，它们只会变得更加重要，成为保护动物免受干旱和极端温度影响的重要气候避难所。

paragraphs.en: Yet, rocky areas are often undervalued as habitat and are rarely protected or managed. As a result, scientists don’t know how quickly these habitats are disappearing. Without greater recognition and action, we risk losing both these habitats and the species that depend on them.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，岩石地区作为栖息地的价值往往被低估，很少受到保护或管理。因此，科学家们不知道这些栖息地消失的速度有多快。如果不加强认识和行动，我们就有可能失去这些栖息地和依赖它们的物种。

paragraphs.en: But not all hope is lost. Our earlier research on Australian farms found that adding surface rocks back into cleared landscapes immediately benefits local wildlife. Within a year, restored rocky areas supported more reptiles and a greater diversity of species, compared to areas without added rock.
paragraphs.zh: 但并非所有的希望都破灭了。我们之前对澳大利亚农场的研究发现，在清理过的土地上重新添加地表岩石会立即造福当地的野生动物。与没有添加岩石的地区相比，在一年之内，恢复的岩石区可以养活更多的爬行动物和更多样的物种。

paragraphs.en:
We still know very little about rocky habitats and the life they sustain. In fact,
new rock-dependent species are constantly being unearthed. So protecting these rich and rugged landscapes is vital to protecting not only species we know, but those yet to be discovered.
paragraphs.zh:
我们对岩石栖息地和它们所维持的生命仍然知之甚少。事实上，
新的依赖岩石的物种不断被发掘出来。因此，保护这些丰富而崎岖的景观不仅对保护我们已知的物种，而且对保护那些尚未被发现的物种至关重要。
